results.title: Tukey reducibility
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For preordered sets $D$ and $E$, $D$ is Tukey reducible to $E$, written $D \le_T E$, if there is a map $f \colon D \to E$ that carries unbounded sets to unbounded sets: for every $A \subseteq D$ with no upper bound in $D$, the image $f[A]$ has no upper bound in $E$.

results.title: Tukey equivalence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Preordered sets $D$ and $E$ are Tukey equivalent (cofinally equivalent), written $D \equiv_T E$, if $D \le_T E$ and $E \le_T D$, where $\le_T$ is Tukey reducibility.

results.title: Cofinal type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A cofinal type is an equivalence class of preordered sets under Tukey equivalence $\equiv_T$, where $D \equiv_T E$ means $D \le_T E$ and $E \le_T D$ (Tukey reducibility in both directions).

results.title: Permuting subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $H$ and $X$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H$ permutes with $X$ when $HX = XH$ as subsets of $G$, where $HX = \{hx : h \in H, x \in X\}$ and $XH = \{xh : x \in X, h \in H\}$.

results.title: Propermutable subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is propermutable in $G$ when there is a subgroup $B$ of $G$ with $G = N_G(H)B$ (every element of $G$ is a product $nb$ with $n$ in the normalizer $N_G(H)$ of $H$ and $b \in B$) such that $H$ permutes with every subgroup $X$ of $B$, that is, $HX = XH$.

results.title: 2-nilpotent groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is $2$-nilpotent when it has a normal subgroup $N$ of finite odd order whose index in $G$ is $2^k$ for some natural number $k$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (statement)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (A. N. Skiba): there exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (statement)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (A. N. Skiba), with the range $1 \le k < n$: let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent.

results.title: Propermutability is not inherited by intermediate subgroups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(a).

results.title: Propermutable subgroups of a non-abelian Sylow 2-subgroup force 2-nilpotency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(b).

results.title: Connectedness in the sense of Hausdorff
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A topological space $G$ is connected in the sense of Hausdorff when it is not the union of two disjoint nonempty closed subsets.

results.title: Arcwise connected space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A topological space $G$ is arcwise connected when for any two points $x, y \in G$ there is a continuous map $\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to G$ with $\gamma(0) = x$ and $\gamma(1) = y$.

results.title: Claim of Scottish Book Problem 160, part (2)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The claim that every metric group $G$ (a group with a metric for which multiplication and inversion are continuous) that is connected in the sense of Hausdorff is arcwise connected.

results.title: Connected metric groups need not be arcwise connected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The claim of part (2) of Scottish Book Problem 160 is false: there is a metric group $G$ (a group with a metric for which multiplication and inversion are continuous) that is connected in the sense of Hausdorff but not arcwise connected, that is, there are points $x, y \in G$ such that no continuous map $\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to G$ has $\gamma(0) = x$ and $\gamma(1) = y$.

results.title: Equal cardinality of an intersection forces containment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of a group $G$ with $H$ finite. If $H \cap K$ has as many elements as $H$, then $H \le K$.

It is the unique…

results.title: Pairing of the Riemannian gradient with a tangent vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold modelled on a complete real normed space, with a Riemannian metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$, and let $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \in M$ and $v \in T_xM$. Then $\langle \operatorname{grad} f(x), v \rangle = df_x(v)$, where $\operatorname{grad} f(x)$ is the Riemannian gradient of $f$ at $x$ and $df_x$ is the differential of $f$ at $x$.

results.title: Characterization of the Riemannian gradient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold modelled on a complete real normed space, with a Riemannian metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$, and let $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \in M$ and $w \in T_xM$. Then the Riemannian gradient $\operatorname{grad} f(x)$ equals $w$ if and only if $\langle w, v \rangle = df_x(v)$ for every $v \in T_xM$, where $df_x$ is the differential of $f$ at $x$.

results.title: Norm of the Riemannian gradient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold modelled on a complete real normed space, with a Riemannian metric, and let $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in M$. With $T_xM$ normed by the metric at $x$, the norm of the Riemannian gradient $\operatorname{grad} f(x)$ equals the operator norm of the differential $df_x : T_xM \to \mathbb{R}$ of $f$ at $x$: $\|\operatorname{grad} f(x)\| = \|df_x\|$. This is the quantity $|\nabla f|(x)$.

results.title: Hudson–Kreitman–Aguadé statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The HKA statistic for `L` loci with polymorphism counts `SA i`, `SB i`, divergences `D i`, parameters `θ i`, `T`, `f` and sample sizes `nA`, `nB`: the sum over loci of the squared standardized deviations of the three counts from their HKA expectations.

results.title: Positivity of the HKA polymorphism variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: HKA's variances are positive in the biological domain: `θ > 0`, `n ≥ 2`.

results.title: Positivity of the HKA divergence variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: HKA's divergence variance is positive for `θ > 0`, `T ≥ 0`, `f > -1`.

results.title: The HKA statistic has mean `3 L` at the true parameters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If every count is square integrable with the HKA mean and variance (as derived above under the neutral model), with `θ i > 0`, `T ≥ 0`, `f > 0` and `nA, nB ≥ 2`, then `E X² = 3 L`.

results.title: HKA's estimating equations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: HKA's estimating equations (Hudson, Kreitman & Aguadé 1987) for parameters `θ i`, `T`, `f` given the counts: the totals over loci of polymorphism in `A`, in `B` and of divergence match their expectations, and at each locus the total of the three counts matches its expectation. (Only `L - 1` of the per-locus equations are independent of the totals.)

results.title: True parameters solve the HKA estimating equations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The true parameters solve HKA's estimating equations at the expected counts.

results.title: Translation invariance of the plus state
results.caption: Theorem
